THE SHARED RESIDUAL FREE INPUT IS NOW A FUNCTION OF ITS ARGUMENTS.  A cut is `residual_<routine>_<depth>_<sha256(alpha-normalised refs; mentions)>`, so two cuts share a symbol IFF they cut the same routine at the same depth with alpha-equal arguments — the registry's stated condition, DECIDED rather than assumed.  Was: the symbol was `residual_<routine>_<depth>`, the arguments were discarded, and the test compared NAME SETS, which carried no argument information to compare.  `EquivPipelineTest` now calls `alignCuts` and, where routine and depth agree but the arguments do not, emits the ARGUMENT EQUIVALENCE as its own prover obligation (`<name>-residual-args-k<k>-<i>.smt2`); an undischarged one fails the cell instead of aliasing two unrelated inputs.
